result.against_which_test: full-backing reserve coverage >=100% of aggregate claims

article_basis: Article 36(1) obligation to constitute and maintain reserve at all times; Article 36(7) aggregate value shall be at least equal to aggregate value of claims against issuer from holders in circulation; Article 36(4)(d) minimum 30% in deposits (context, not threshold for this case)
tail_convention: Coverage ratio is higher-is-better metric. LOW tail (low coverage) is adverse. This test examines adverse LOW tail by checking if coverage <100% fails. Does not examine favorable high tail.
weakest_point: Market values of reserve assets assumed observable without bid-ask; does not test liquidity maturity buckets or custody segregation; uses single point-in-time valuation, not average over day

case_name: Own-funds computation - ART percentage-of-reserve and fixed minimum

average_reserve_6m_daily_close.definition: average amount at end of each calendar day over preceding six months per Article 35(1) second subpara

result.regulatory_verdict_sig: inadequate against Article 45(5) 3% test, would need additional 250,000 EUR
result.against_which_test: own-funds highest-of fixed minimum EUR 350k, percentage of average reserve (2% or 3% if significant), quarter fixed overheads

article_basis: Article 35(1) first subparagraph points (a) EUR 350k, (b) 2% of average amount of reserve assets referred to in Article 36, (c) quarter fixed overheads; Article 35(1) second subpara definition average end of each calendar day over preceding six months; Article 45(5) percentage set at 3% for issuers of significant asset-referenced tokens; Article 35(2) composition CET1; Article 35(3) and (5) supervisory add-on up to +20% and stress-based +20-40% (percentages stated from EUR-Lex verification)
tail_convention: Own funds coverage is higher-is-better metric. LOW tail (low own funds vs requirement) is adverse. This test examines adverse LOW tail by checking max requirement and comparing actual own funds below threshold fails. Does not examine favorable high tail.
weakest_point: Fixed overheads calculation per Article 67(3) delegated not detailed; average reserve calculation assumes daily data available; does not include potential supervisory add-ons under Article 35(3) and 35(5) which could increase requirement by 20-40%

case_name: Stressed-coverage case - reserve decline with haircuts

inputs.stress_scenario: Interest rate shock + credit spread widening

result.against_which_test: full-backing Article 36(7) aggregate value at least equal to claims, under stressed values; also triggers recovery plan assessment per Article 46

article_basis: Article 36(7) full backing test; Article 35(5) regular stress testing including interest rate shocks; Article 45(4) liquidity stress testing for significant tokens; Article 46 recovery plan when fails to comply with reserve requirements
tail_convention: Coverage ratio is higher-is-better. LOW tail is adverse. Stress test examines adverse LOW tail by applying negative haircuts to reserve assets (decline in value). Explicitly does NOT examine favorable HIGH tail (increase in reserve value) which would incorrectly show improvement. Adverse direction correctly chosen as reserve decrease.
weakest_point: Haircuts 0% and 10% are illustrative scenario, not regulatory prescribed; does not model correlation between assets or de-peg of token reference; does not include 30% minimum deposits in credit institutions per Article 36(4)(d) liquidity requirement

computation.step_1_obligation: Holder claim per Article 49(4) / Article 39: redeem at par in funds other than e-money, 500,000 EUR
computation.step_7_match_principle: Issuance/redemption matched by increase/decrease in reserve per Article 36(6)

result.against_which_test: redemption at par obligation per Article 49(4) EMT and Article 36(6) matching principle, plus full-backing Article 36(7) after operation

article_basis: Article 49(3) issuance at par and on receipt of funds; Article 49(4) redemption at any time at par in funds other than electronic money; Article 36(6) issuance and redemption always matched by corresponding increase/decrease in reserve; Article 36(7) post-redemption reserve still >= claims; Article 39 rights of redemption for ART holders (general)
tail_convention: Coverage after redemption is higher-is-better. LOW tail (coverage dropping below 100% after redemption) is adverse. This test examines adverse LOW tail by verifying coverage remains >=100% after paying redemption. Does not examine favorable high tail. For redemption amount itself, higher payout is adverse for issuer liquidity, so test examines high payout amount as adverse.
weakest_point: Assumes instant settlement from cash bucket without selling bonds at discount; does not model intraday liquidity or 30% deposit minimum; assumes no fees; real redemption may require pro-rata asset sale per investment policy Article 38
